Maria: Ran a multi-cluster simulator sweep (affinity weights + token budgets) this morning — hit a regression when cross-zone spillover starts to become non-trivial.

Maria: Summary: sim-id sim-1969-03, config -> affinity_weight=0.65, cross_zone_penalty=0.25, token_budget_per_request=48, batch_window_ms=6

Maria: Profiler excerpt:
```
avg_latency_ms: 34.2
p95_latency_ms: 142.8
p99_latency_ms: 310.1
kv_cache_hit_rate: {zoneA: 0.78, zoneB: 0.41}
evictions/s: {zoneA: 2.3, zoneB: 18.7}
batch_size_mean: 10.4
```
Maria: Key observation: once spillover from zoneA->zoneB > ~15%, zoneB's KV hit rate collapses, eviction rate spikes, and p95 jumps — looks like cache thrash + different kernel selection path on zoneB nodes.

Alex: How many simulated hosts per zone? sample size? :eyes:

Maria: 48 hosts total (24/zone), synthetic traffic matching real seq-len dist; warmup 10m, then 30m steady. We injected a top-1% spike to force spillover.

Jordan: Did the runtime pick a different GEMM kernel for zoneB hardware? We had that fallback change in last rollout.

Samir: I suspect batching shape changes too. When KV hit-rate drops, effective sequence prefix lengths change and we start seeing smaller micro-batches + more context copies. Cache pressure + smaller batches -> worse throughput.

perf-bot: ALERT: Regression detected for sim-1969-03 vs baseline sim-1968-21 -> p95 +18% (link: https://perf.internal/sim/1969-03) :warning:

Lee: Could be two orthogonal issues: (1) kernel selection fallback path uses slower matmul for short sequences, (2) KV eviction policy is global-per-node and doesn't respect zone-local affinity. When spillover places extra shard load on zoneB, it never prefetches.

Alex: Can you paste the kernel selection log chunk? small snippet is fine.

Maria: Kernel log snippet:
```
[2026-03-18 09:12:42] model=llama-7b kernel=matmul_opt_v2 sequence_len=32 host=zoneB-12 chosen=true perf_est=1.2
[2026-03-18 09:12:42] model=llama-7b kernel=matmul_generic sequence_len=8 host=zoneB-12 chosen=true perf_est=0.9
[2026-03-18 09:12:43] decision=fallthrough->matmul_generic reason=short_seq_and_low_mem
```

Jordan: That fallthrough line looks like the new heuristic that treats short sequences as "low-memory" and forces the generic kernel. If generic kernel is slower on our GPUs for these batch shapes, that explains p95.

Samir: Quick experiment idea: (A) force old kernel selection policy on zoneB and re-run, (B) increase token_budget_per_request to 64 for spillover requests so KV cache retains more prefixes. Try A first — cheaper.

Lee: Also add a per-zone soft-reserve cache quota: when receiving cross-zone requests, prefer not to evict local hot prefixes below a threshold. Should be small change in eviction policy.

Maria: I'll run A+B in parallel sims tonight and post results. For reproducibility I'm checking in the simulator config under: infra/sim/configs/sim-1969-03.yaml (PR incoming).

Alex: If A fixes latency but increases token cost, we need to weigh cost vs SLA. Keep the perf-bot screenshot in the thread for triage.

perf-bot: NOTE: Regression ticket created -> #perf/regressions/1969-03 (assigned to @Jordan)

Jordan: Acknowledged. I'll take the kernel path first. If that doesn't close it, I'll pair with Samir on cache policy changes. :thumbsup:

Maria: Thanks — I'll drop the full raw trace and KV eviction counters once sims finish (ETA ~8h).
